newsitem.title: USA: Current US growth may not be sustainable--S.F. Fed.
newsitem.headline: Current US growth may not be sustainable--S.F. Fed.

text.p: The U.S. economy has been expanding at a healthy pace, but its current rate of growth might not be sustainable without sparking inflation in the long run, said the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Robert Parry.
"Is this (economic) performance sustainable? I'm doubtful that it is.

"If traditional relationships hold, we wouldn't expect the level of resource utilization ... to be sustainable without inflation becoming a problem," Parry told an audience of business executives in Fairbanks, Alaska on Tuesday.
"The longer-run concern about inflation remains a live issue," Parry added.
The San Francisco Fed chief, who spent the day in Alaska, mostly reiterated his earlier remarks made at a breakfast in Anchorage during a second speech in Fairbanks in the afternoon.
A copy of Parry's speech was made available in New York by the San Francisco Fed.
